allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking gives leverage-points the whole-system view needed to find where a small intervention can actually shift behavior.
allies.source_quote: Systems thinking, the foundation of LPs, is about seeing interrelationships and patterns of change.
allies.affinity_rationale: Leverage points require 'drawing on diverse models to fully understand the integrated ecosystem' — systems thinking provides the map of interconnections within which leverage points are identified.
allies.activation_condition: When identifying high-impact interventions requires mapping the full system of interconnections rather than analyzing isolated components

allies.rationale_text: Prioritization helps leverage-points convert structural insight into a disciplined decision about what to do now and what to leave alone.
allies.source_quote: Problem solvers should focus on issues that have the biggest impact and that they can actually influence.
allies.affinity_rationale: MECE decomposition 'provides the logical and structural rigor to identify leverage points effectively' — ensures the problem breakdown covers every aspect without overlap.
allies.activation_condition: When multiple potential intervention points exist and structural decomposition is needed to determine which elements are truly critical versus merely visible

allies.rationale_text: First-principles-thinking helps leverage-points look beneath conventional surface fixes to the deeper system element that truly governs outcomes.
allies.source_quote: This approach ... strips away assumptions to leave only core facts and desired outcomes.
allies.affinity_rationale: Described as 'highly synergistic' — first-principles 'strips away assumptions to leave only core facts and desired outcomes, allowing the user to forge a new solution instead of following conventional, lower-leverage methods'.
allies.activation_condition: When conventional intervention approaches are low-leverage and finding the highest-impact point requires decomposing the problem to fundamental truths rather than following inherited frameworks

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias can make leverage-point selection reflect the analyst's preferred intervention instead of the system's real sensitivity.
antagonists.source_quote: leverage-points conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when leverage point identification is driven by confirming the analyst's preferred intervention rather than systematic sensitivity testing.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Focusing analysis only on data that supports the initial assumed leverage point rather than seeking disconfirming evidence — directly corrupts the identification process.
antagonists.activation_condition: When leverage point identification is driven by the analyst's preferred intervention rather than systematic sensitivity testing across the full system

structured_tensions.tension_text: Leverage-points conflicts with optionality when continuous branching delays commitment to the highest-impact intervention.
structured_tensions.source_quote: leverage-points vs optionality: leverage-points conflicts with optionality (optionality) when continuous branching delays commitment to the highest-impact intervention.
